lines: We used to think that our brains could not change.
But now scientists know that they can.
A scientist named Richard Davidson says that our brains are shaped by repeating the same thoughts again and again.
He explains, “Being happy is like learning to play the cello.
If we practice, we can get better.”
In other words, we can train our brains to feel more thankful, relaxed, or brave.
When we repeat the same thoughts and actions, our brain cells work together.
As these brain cells continue to work together, their connections get stronger.
Over time, these strong connections help us form new habits and change our brains.
This idea is supported by another scientist, Donald Hebb.
He says, “Brain cells that work together connect together.”
If we keep thinking positive thoughts, our brains can become happier.
